summary: Pass: the change makes all four page edits and meets every criterion. I checked it by running `cargo run -p xtask -- site` and `cargo test -p xtask` on this snapshot, and both succeeded. Fmt, clippy and the full test suite come from Athena's recorded checks. The edits: (1) the findings are renumbered f1, f2, f3, with no claims changed; (2) the study-id paragraph moved out of the header into an 'About this page' note after the claims, starting 'This page's study id'; (3) one claim-linked sentence saying what firstmate is now comes before 'Words used first'; (4) Next steps now has `./setup.sh` and `athena ask "add a changelog"`, which match README.md Quick start. The new test in xtask/tests/site_page.rs renders the real page and checks each edit. It would fail on the old code (ids f1, f3, f4; study id in the header; no what-is sentence). All changed files are on the deliverables list, and the changelog has an entry. There are two nits: the README check matches the commands anywhere in README.md, not only in Quick start, and the new sentence largely repeats the paragraph below it.
